content.text:
This is your first easing lesson. In Mentor Practice I found 11 keyframe pairs that need easing, spread across 6 layers. One of them is half done: Subtitle's Opacity is already eased at its first key, but its last key is still linear.

I'd suggest starting with **Title**. It has four pairs: two Position moves, plus Scale and Opacity.

I'm leaving out two layers for now:
- **Old Take** is hidden, so I'll skip it unless you want it.
- **Icon** is a precomp. I can't see inside precomps yet, so I'm not saying it's fine.

Do you want to start with Title, or pick a different layer?

Title it is. This is your comp at 1 s, partway through Title's first move.

From 0.5 s to 1.5 s, Title moves at one speed the whole way, then stops dead at 1.5 s: that's linear, and it's why it looks mechanical. Easing slows it out of each key and into the next. With Title's keys showing (U), select both keys of a pair and choose **Animation > Keyframe Assistant > Easy Ease** (F9); the diamonds turn into hourglasses.

Ease Title's two Position moves (0.5 s to 1.5 s and 1.5 s to 3 s), plus its Scale and its Opacity (both 0.5 s to 1.5 s), then say done.
The active comp right now isn't Mentor Practice, so I can't check your work there. Switch back to **Mentor Practice** and say done again.
